correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the lower bound to exact crown distances. For a_i,a_j in one class, strong resolution requires set-distances 1 and 3; the unique distance-3 vertex from a_i is b_i, forcing a singleton matched vertex for every pair and hence at least r-1 singleton B-classes for r A-vertices grouped together. Summation yields at least n classes. The displayed n-class partition is verified case-by-case. The packaged checker independently validates the construction for n=3..12 and exhaustively excludes fewer than n classes for n=3,4,5.

value.rationale: The crown graph is a standard highly symmetric bipartite family and strong partition dimension is a natural location invariant. Generic 2-antipodal theory gives only 2 <= pd_s <= n+1, so the exact value n closes a substantial structural gap. The singleton-antipode charging lemma is reusable and explains why a matching strong resolving graph can still force linearly many partition classes.
